fix_applied.location: lib/letflow/service_catalog.ex, delete/1 and new private delete_entry/1 helper
fix_applied.after: %Entry{} = entry -> case referencing_active_definitions(...) do [] -> delete_entry(entry), where delete_entry/1 does `case Repo.delete(entry) do {:ok, _deleted} -> :ok; {:error, _changeset} -> {:error, :not_found} end rescue Ecto.StaleEntryError -> {:error, :not_found} end`
fix_applied.rationale: Repo.delete/1 matches on primary key alone (Entry has no optimistic-lock field), so a row deleted concurrently between the top-of-function Repo.get/2 and this call raises Ecto.StaleEntryError rather than returning {:error, changeset}. The bare match could not catch either outcome. The new delete_entry/1 both passes through Repo.delete/1's real {:ok, _} | {:error, changeset} result (matching the lib/letflow/webhooks.ex:270 Letflow.Webhooks.delete/2 precedent cited in the prior review) and explicitly rescues Ecto.StaleEntryError, translating the concurrent-delete race to {:error, :not_found} -- consistent with get_for_tenant/2's and update_scope/2's own not-found handling. The @spec on delete/1 already declared {:error, :not_found} as a valid return, so no @spec/@doc change was needed.
fix_applied.scope: Only delete/1's success-path delete call and the new delete_entry/1 private helper changed. get_for_tenant/2, list_for_tenant/2, register/1, update_scope/2, referencing_active_definitions/2, query_referencing_definitions/2, and the Lookup implementation are byte-for-byte unchanged (see the diff -- 17 insertions, 2 deletions, all within delete/1's success branch and the new helper).
